Maintenance Report — MNT-0106-002

Asset: WELL-0106 (NE-07 Well 106, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 25 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 12 Mar 2024 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 385 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0106-0010 on 2024-02-22 Report written: 13 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0106-0010 showed the wellhead at 17.4 °C with the air at 12.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0106-002 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0106-006

Asset: WELL-0106 (NE-07 Well 106, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 08 Jun 2024 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 22 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0106-0025 on 2024-06-06 Report written: 09 Jun 2024

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0106-0025 at 08:15 on 2024-06-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.2% of the pad area, estimated 1.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 249 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 199 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0106-006 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.24% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0106-009

Asset: WELL-0106 (NE-07 Well 106, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 28 Dec 2024 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2025 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 250 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0106-0054 on 2024-12-26 Report written: 09 Jan 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0106-0054 showed the wellhead at 6.7 °C with the air at 6.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0106 (NE-07 Well 106, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 13 Jun 2025 08:00 · Finished: 14 Jun 2025 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 27 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0106-0078 on 2025-06-12 Report written: 15 Jun 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0106-0078 at 14:30 on 2025-06-12 found crude oil on the pad: about 0.6% of the pad area, estimated 0.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 249 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 199 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste
